description: A studio distribution executive must approve the final release package for a documentary being submitted to an international film festival, including territorial access, music, publicity credits, and accessibility deliverables.

shared_context.S1: The documentary 'After the Flood' is being prepared for the Meridian International Film Festival.
shared_context.S2: The festival will receive a public screening file and a password-protected press-screening file.
shared_context.S3: The current draft release sheet lists worldwide access, the cue 'Low Tide,' the working title 'River After Rain,' and optional accessibility materials.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final approval decision for the release package.
shared_context.S5: As part of the standard release meeting, the rights, music, publicity, and accessibility leads each review the package before Mara locks it.

PF1.text: Jonah confirmed with the archive this week that the license for the documentary's archival interview permits festival screening and password-protected press access only in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland; it forbids public online access and access in all other territories. Jonah has not copied the confirmation into the release sheet yet because the archive's signed email arrived after the last package revision.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the publisher that the current cue 'Low Tide' is cleared for only 30 seconds, while the alternate cue 'Northbound' is cleared for the full 46-second trailer segment. She has not replaced the cue name in the package because the editor delivered the latest cut after her clearance check.

PF3.text: Owen has the filmmaker's signed publicity approval requiring the title 'After the Flood' and the credit line 'A film by Nia Okafor'; the working title and generic credit remain in the draft because the signed approval arrived during the poster revision.

PF4.text: Sofia confirmed with the festival's access coordinator that the final submission must include open English captions and a separate audio-description track; the coordinator will reject a package containing either deliverable as optional. Sofia has not updated the release checklist because the festival issued this ingest requirement in a separate accessibility email.

acceptance_conditions: Access must be limited to the four territories permitted by the archival license.
The music cue must be changed to the cue cleared for the full 46-second segment.
The approved title and filmmaker credit must match the signed publicity approval.
The package must include open English captions.
The package must include a separate audio-description track.
A rights-restriction commitment must be logged.
A music-clearance commitment must be logged.
An accessibility-delivery commitment must be logged.

content_checks.C3: decisions['approved_title'] == 'After the Flood' and decisions['credit_line'] == 'A film by Nia Okafor'
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'rights_restriction' and c['target'] == 'archival interview' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'music_clearance' and c['target'] == 'Northbound' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft says worldwide access, but PF1 changes the permitted territory list to exactly the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland and requires a rights-restriction record.
PF2 changes the music choice from 'Low Tide,' cleared for only 30 seconds, to 'Northbound,' cleared for the exact 46-second segment, and requires a music-clearance record.
PF3 changes the approved title from 'River After Rain' to exactly 'After the Flood' and changes the credit line to exactly 'A film by Nia Okafor'.
PF4 changes captions and audio description from optional materials to two required deliverables and requires an accessibility-delivery record.
